_comment: UNDERTOW teaser cue sheet — the 30-second cut of the sinking, built for release rather than for the episode. Same doctrine as the scene it is cut from: this document IS the teaser, build-scene.py renders its mix and build-sequence.py cuts its picture, and neither holds any teaser data of its own. DISTRIBUTION IS PIPELINE: the lesson taken from studying commercial AI-film products is that poster, teaser and release metadata are pipeline steps, not afterthoughts — but here they are authored as cue sheets and briefs rather than clicked through a wizard. Every visual in this cut is an existing episode plate; the teaser cost zero generation credits by construction.
title: UNDERTOW — series teaser (30s)
_ranks_comment: The full episode ladder minus nothing: the teaser IS the descent, compressed. Ordered, because the descent interpolates POSITION on it.
_beats_comment: The scene's 72-second arc compressed to 30 without changing its shape: air, the flinch, the fall, panic, and then the long settle to 34 BPM. The teaser ends where the episode's thesis is — held at 34 — rather than resolving, because a teaser's job is to open a question.

_score_comment: The composed cue (build-score.py --cue ep1-teaser): CALL over the Eye, the impact hit, CALL answered over the ocean turn, and the ANSWER landing its first note exactly on the title card.
_tone_comment: The thing in the water, arriving under the second card and running out under the title. No fade_out: the last thing the teaser leaves in the room is the deep, breathing.
_shots_comment: Twelve shots, every frame an existing episode plate or a locally-rendered card — the teaser spends nothing. Native speed wherever an excerpt can cover the window (the v2 lesson: retiming is where slapstick comes from); the only retimed shots are ones whose whole action must land inside the window. The Eye Rule holds here too: brown/hidden eyes until 21.5, blue only underwater.

_cards_comment: The teaser's three text cards, authored here as data and rendered by build-cards.py — same rule as everything else: a person edits this file, not a script. Near-black with the faintest light-from-above gradient; the title card alone gets the blue glow from below, because that is the show's key image (the boy on the pool floor, lit from beneath).

duck._comment: Two silences, both earned: the pre-buzzer drop into his head, and the title drop — the world ducks under the title so the last ten seconds belong to a 34 BPM heart and the tone. Silence is a resource. The trailing 30.0 point exists because interp holds the RIGHT edge at 1.0 past the last point; without it the title duck would silently release.

_events_comment: Three events, all inherited from the episode's spot placements: the flinch, the impact, the scream. The teaser adds nothing the episode does not have — v3's lesson standing guard.
